_meta.corporation_charter: Royal Charter of the Corporation of Madras, 29 September 1688 (East India Company) — the OLDEST municipal corporation in India; modern statute: the Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 (TN Act IV of 1919, orig. Madras City Municipal Corporation Act).
_meta.what: The governance-fragmentation dossier for Chennai: EVERY body that took a Twelfth-Schedule (or core municipal) function away from the elected Greater Chennai Corporation, pre AND post 1991, recorded on the analytical axis of WHO DECIDED. Each entry = {body, what, how (enabling instrument named, decided_by), why (stated rationale + real political economy), era}. Companion to corporation_history.json (lineage), service_providers.json (who-provides scorecard), privatization_map.json + contractualization_map.json (the private/contract carve-outs).
_meta.thesis: Chennai is the central irony of the atlas: it holds the OLDEST corporation in India (Madras, 1688 — older than Calcutta, Bombay, every other by ~two centuries) yet is among the MOST hollowed. Age did not protect devolution. The carve-out is not colonial; it is overwhelmingly a POST-1960s state-government project — water to Metrowater (1978), planning/land to CMDA (1971/72 Act), transport to MTC and then the CMRL SPV (2007), housing-the-poor to the Slum Clearance Board (1970) and Housing Board (1961). And in the 2020s the corporation's last large in-house function — conservancy/solid-waste — was itself privatised: 10 of 15 GCC zones handed to Urbaser-Sumeet and Ramky. The decision-maker, in every single case, is the STATE government in Fort St George (or the colonial Company before it), NEVER the elected city. The 2011 'Greater Chennai' expansion was itself an executive notification under the 1919 Act, not a fresh statute — even the corporation's own boundary is drawn by the state, not the council.

decided_by_legend.colonial: Decided by the East India Company / colonial state (pre-1947 charters and acts carried forward).
decided_by_legend.centre: Decided by the Union Parliament / Government of India.
decided_by_legend.state: Decided by the Government of Tamil Nadu (Legislature or executive) at Fort St George.
decided_by_legend.city: Decided by the elected Corporation of Chennai itself. (Note: NO carve-out in this dossier was decided by the city — that is the finding.)

analytical_frames.depoliticisation_ghosh: Anwesha Ghosh ('Municipal Calcutta', UofT 2021; 'The Improvement Regime', CSSH 2025): the improvement-trust / development-authority is the instrument for lifting 'technical' development OUT of elected municipal politics and handing it to appointed technocrats. CMDA is the Madras instance — though Madras notably had NO classic colonial Improvement Trust, so the depoliticising body arrived LATE, as a post-Independence state creation (TNTCP Act 1971).
analytical_frames.land_financialisation: Ghosh's 'recoupment': the development authority holds and monetises city land. CMDA, as planning + land-acquisition authority for the Chennai Metropolitan Area, and CMRL/Smart City SPVs (transit-oriented development, land value capture) are the rentier machines.
analytical_frames.neoliberal_conditionality_cooper: Melinda Cooper ('Counterrevolution', 2024): privatisation of public goods and the SPV/PPP form as counterrevolution against democratic claims on the economy; austerity-extravagance (starve the elected body of funds/functions while lavishing capital on off-budget SPVs and concessions). CMRL (JICA-funded SPV, off the municipal books), Smart City Ltd (Mission conditionality forcing an SPV), and the SWM concessions are the Chennai instances.
analytical_frames.caste_labour_offloading: Ambedkar's 'division of labour is also a division of labourers': Chennai privatised 10 of 15 SWM zones (Urbaser-Sumeet 7, Ramky 4), transferring its predominantly-Dalit, predominantly-women conservancy workforce from GCC rolls to private operators — extinguishing a long struggle for permanency and CUTTING take-home pay (~Rs 11,730 -> ~Rs 9,000/mo). The hollowing of the elected body lands hardest on the caste-coded front line.

_meta.schema: { body, abbr, function_taken, twelfth_schedule_items, what, how:{instrument, act_no, year, decided_by, instrument_type}, why:{stated, real_political_economy[]}, era, verify, source }
_meta.status: Authored 2026-06-09. Acts/years verified against data/laws/chennai/manifest.md (CMC Act 1919 = TN Act IV of 1919; TNTCP 1971 = TN Act 35 of 1972; CMWSSB 1978 = TN Act 28 of 1978 — all 'Verified' in the manifest against the statute PDFs) and against the 74th-Amendment constitutional layer. Bodies NOT in the laws/chennai PDF set (Slum Clearance Board, Housing Board, MTC, CMRL, Smart City Ltd, TANGEDCO) are recorded from the public institutional record with verify:true where the exact act-number/year is not confirmed against the gazette. NO fabrication; uncertain fields flagged, not guessed.
_meta.headline: Chennai = oldest corporation in India (1688), among the most hollowed. ~10 carve-out bodies/instruments; ALL decided by state or colonial power, NONE by the elected city. Split: ~3 pre-1991, ~7 post-1991 (or post-1991-active), with the 2020s SWM-zone privatisation hollowing even the corporation's flagship in-house function.

carve_outs.function_taken: Urban & metropolitan planning; master plan / detailed development plans; land-use & building regulation; development control; planning permission; land acquisition for planning across the Chennai Metropolitan Area
carve_outs.what: Statutory planning authority for the Chennai Metropolitan Area (CMA). Prepares and enforces the Master Plan and Detailed Development Plans, grants planning permission, regulates land-use and zoning, and acquires/monetises land for planning — functions a corporation elsewhere (e.g. AMC, BMC) substantially keeps in-house. GCC is left with only local building-plan approval.

how.instrument: The Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, 1971
how.act_no: Tamil Nadu Act 35 of 1972 (the 1971 Bill received President's assent 24 Nov 1972)

why.stated: Coordinated, scientific metropolitan planning across a region wider than the city limits; the elected corporation's jurisdiction was deemed too narrow for regional master-planning and the work too 'technical' for council politics.
real_political_economy: Depoliticisation (Ghosh): planning and land — the rent-rich functions — lifted OUT of the elected body and handed to a state-appointed authority; Madras had no classic colonial Improvement Trust, so the depoliticising body arrived LATE, as a post-Independence state creation, but does the same work.

Land financialisation / recoupment: CMDA holds land-acquisition and development-control powers across the CMA — the planning-and-land rentier machine Ghosh describes; control of where value is created and captured sits with the state, not the elected city.

The 2022 Second Amendment (TN Act, 22 Jun 2022) adds Urban Development Authorities for Urban Planning Areas — extending the state-appointed-authority model further, again by state law, not municipal devolution.

carve_outs.source: data/laws/chennai/manifest.md (TNTCP 1971 = TN Act 35 of 1972, Verified); India Code handle 13338; CMDA portal.

carve_outs.body: Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (Chennai Metrowater)
carve_outs.function_taken: Water supply (domestic, industrial, commercial) AND sewerage / sewage treatment for the Chennai Metropolitan Area — the single biggest carve-out from the GCC
carve_outs.what: Exclusive statutory board for planning, development, operation, regulation and tariff-setting of water supply and sewerage across the CMA. Water (#5) and sanitation/sewerage (#6) — the highest-value daily-provisioning functions — sit entirely OUTSIDE the elected corporation, unlike Mumbai/Ahmedabad/Kolkata where the corporation runs water in-house.

how.instrument: The Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1978
how.act_no: Tamil Nadu Act 28 of 1978 (President's assent 8 Jun 1978; first pub. TN Govt Gazette Extraordinary 14 Jun 1978)

why.stated: A dedicated, technically-specialised metropolitan utility to plan and run water/sewerage at metropolitan scale, protect public health, and finance large bulk-water and treatment capital works beyond the corporation's means.
real_political_economy: The textbook carve-out (Ghosh's depoliticisation): the most valuable, most rate-able 12th-Schedule function affirmatively LEGISLATED out of the elected body into a purpose-built state board — a deliberate write-out, not a gap.

Cooper's austerity-extravagance: capital-intensive bulk water (desalination, Veeranam, Krishna water) is run by a state board that can carry debt and court external/IFI finance off the municipal balance sheet, while the elected city is denied the function and its revenue.

Accountability removed from the ballot: a Chennai resident cannot vote on water tariff or coverage — the board answers to the state government, not the council; service to the colony vs the settlement is a state-board calculation.

carve_outs.source: data/laws/chennai/manifest.md (CMWSSB 1978 = TN Act 28 of 1978, Verified); India Code handle 13109; CAG copy.

carve_outs.body: Tamil Nadu Slum Clearance Board (now Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board)
carve_outs.function_taken: Slum clearance, in-situ upgradation, resettlement and tenement housing for the urban poor — slum improvement (#10) and urban poverty alleviation (#11)
carve_outs.what: State board that identifies, clears, rebuilds and resettles slums and builds tenements for the urban poor across Chennai (and TN). The 'housing-the-poor' function — and the politically charged power to evict and relocate settlements (often to the city's far periphery, e.g. Kannagi Nagar, Perumbakkam) — sits with a state board, not the elected city. Renamed/restructured as the TN Urban Habitat Development Board (2021).

how.instrument: The Tamil Nadu Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1971 — the board itself constituted by Government order in 1970; later restructured as TNUHDB (2021, Government order)
how.act_no: Tamil Nadu Act 11 of 1971 (Slum Areas Improvement & Clearance Act); board constituted 1970

why.stated: Specialised agency to clear unsanitary slums, improve living conditions, and provide tenement housing and basic services to the urban poor at scale.
real_political_economy: Caste/labour offloading: the management of the city's poorest, most-Dalit settlements — eviction and peripheral resettlement that frees up central land — is handed to a state board insulated from the local electorate that those residents could otherwise hold to account.

Land financialisation: 'clearance' liberates valuable central-city land for higher-value use while pushing the poor to distant resettlement colonies (the recoupment logic); the relocation map is a land-value map.
Depoliticisation: the most contentious distributive question in the city — who is evicted, who is rehoused, where — is removed from council debate to a state-appointed board.

carve_outs.source: TNSCB/TNUHDB official record; TN Slum Areas (Improvement & Clearance) Act 1971 (act-no./constitution-year cross-check pending against gazette).

carve_outs.function_taken: Planned housing development, housing schemes and neighbourhood/township development in and around Chennai
carve_outs.what: State housing agency that develops housing colonies, neighbourhood schemes and townships (e.g. Anna Nagar, Ashok Nagar, K.K. Nagar) — assembling and developing land for housing, a land-and-development function exercised by the state rather than the elected city.

how.instrument: The Tamil Nadu State Housing Board Act, 1961

why.stated: A dedicated state agency to address the post-Independence urban housing shortage by planning and building housing schemes at scale.
real_political_economy: Land financialisation / recoupment (Ghosh): a state body assembles, develops and disposes of land for housing — capturing the development value — outside any municipal-electoral check.
An early (pre-CMDA) instance of the state holding the land-and-development function in Madras; the development-authority logic predates the planning authority here.
Depoliticisation of who gets housed where, a distributive question removed from the elected council to the state board.

carve_outs.source: TN State Housing Board Act 1961 (TNHB official history); act-no./year cross-check pending against India Code.

carve_outs.function_taken: City bus / public road transport — a Twelfth-Schedule public-amenity function (bus stops/public transport, #17 family)
carve_outs.what: State-owned road-transport corporation running Chennai's city bus network. Urban bus transport — which a few corporations (Mumbai's BEST, Ahmedabad's AMTS) run as a municipal undertaking — is in Chennai a state government company, entirely outside the GCC.

how.instrument: Incorporated as a government company under the Companies Act (state-owned road transport undertaking, successor to Pallavan Transport Corporation, est. 1972; reorganised/renamed MTC 1994), operating under the framework of the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950 / Motor Vehicles Act
how.act_no: Government company under the Companies Act; sector framework: Road Transport Corporations Act 1950 (Central Act 64 of 1950)

why.stated: Professional, network-scale public bus operation across the metropolitan area, run by a specialised transport undertaking rather than a municipality.
real_political_economy: Transport — a daily-life function and a patronage/employment estate — held by the state, never devolved to the elected city; the bus you ride answers to the state transport department, not your councillor.

Cooper: the loss-making, labour-heavy bus operation is parked in a state company perpetually dependent on state subsidy, while the rent-rich transit mode (metro) is built in a separate, capital-favoured SPV (CMRL).
Chennai never built a municipal transport undertaking on the BEST/AMTS model — the function originated outside the city and stayed there.

carve_outs.source: MTC Chennai official record (Pallavan Transport Corp 1972 -> MTC 1994); Road Transport Corporations Act 1950; service_providers.json (city_bus = MTC, state_dept).

carve_outs.function_taken: Urban rail mass-transit (metro) — capital-intensive transit and its associated transit-oriented real-estate / land value capture
carve_outs.what: Special-purpose vehicle that builds and operates the Chennai Metro. An off-the-municipal-books SPV financing the city's most capital-intensive transit asset, with associated transit-oriented development / property monetisation — the rent-rich transit mode, structurally separated from the elected city and from the loss-making bus (MTC).

how.instrument: Incorporated as a special-purpose vehicle (government company under the Companies Act), originally a 50:50 Government of India / Government of Tamil Nadu joint venture; JICA-funded; project sanctioned under the Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act / Metro Railways (Operation & Maintenance) Act framework
how.act_no: Government company under the Companies Act, 1956 (incorporated 2007); sector framework: Metro Railways (O&M) Act 2002, Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act 1978

why.stated: A dedicated, professionally-run, ring-fenced entity able to raise large external (JICA) capital and execute a technically-complex metro project on a financeable balance sheet.
real_political_economy: Cooper's counterrevolution/austerity-extravagance: the SPV form keeps a multi-billion asset OFF the municipal (and partly off the state) books, lavishing capital on the prestige mode while the elected city is starved of both the function and the revenue.

Land financialisation (Ghosh's recoupment, modernised): metro projects monetise station-area land via transit-oriented development and value capture — a rentier machine controlled by a Centre-State SPV, not the elected city.

Depoliticisation by corporate form: an SPV answers to its board and lenders, not an electorate; the citizen cannot vote on the metro the way the colonial Improvement Trust answered to no municipal vote.
The metro that runs past the bus you actually ride: capital favours the rent-rich SPV mode over the labour-heavy state bus (MTC).

carve_outs.source: privatization_map.json / service_providers.json (metro = CMRL, spv); CMRL incorporated 2007 (GoI-TN 50:50 JV), JICA-funded; Metro Railways O&M Act 2002.

carve_outs.function_taken: Area-based 'smart city' development, urban-infrastructure project execution and digital/IoT city management within designated zones — executive control over selected urban-development functions
carve_outs.what: A special-purpose vehicle created to receive and spend Smart Cities Mission funds and execute area-based development and pan-city projects — a parallel, board-run channel for urban development that sits beside (and partly displaces) the elected corporation's project role.

how.instrument: Incorporated as a special-purpose vehicle (government company under the Companies Act) as the mandatory implementation vehicle of the Smart Cities Mission, launched by the Government of India in 2015; SPV constituted ~2016
how.act_no: Government company under the Companies Act, 2013; programme: Smart Cities Mission (MoHUA, GoI, 2015) — Mission guidelines, not a statute

why.stated: A dedicated, ring-fenced, professionally-managed vehicle to deliver Mission-funded smart-city projects with operational and financial autonomy.
real_political_economy: Neoliberal conditionality (Cooper): the Smart Cities Mission MANDATED an SPV as the precondition for central funds — the corporate form imposed top-down as the price of money, structurally bypassing the elected council. Central conditionality, not city choice.
Depoliticisation: an unelected company board (with private and parastatal nominees) directs spending on the city's marquee projects, removing them from council deliberation.

Cooper's counterrevolution: the SPV is the institutional template for converting public urban development into a board-run, finance-disciplined enterprise — democracy's claim on the city's development budget displaced by corporate governance.

carve_outs.source: Smart Cities Mission (MoHUA, 2015) SPV requirement; Chennai Smart City Ltd (CSCL) constitution ~2016; exact incorporation date/CIN cross-check pending.

carve_outs.body: Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation
carve_outs.function_taken: Electricity generation and distribution to the city (NOT a Twelfth-Schedule municipal function — recorded for completeness as a state-held daily-provisioning function)
carve_outs.what: State-owned utility supplying electricity to Chennai. Electricity distribution is not a 12th-Schedule item, so this is not a devolution failure in the strict sense; recorded to complete the picture of how much daily provisioning sits with the state rather than the elected city. (Notable contrast: in Ahmedabad/Kolkata/Mumbai-suburbs power is PRIVATE; in Chennai it remains a STATE utility.)

how.instrument: Constituted on the unbundling of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board under the Electricity Act, 2003; TANGEDCO formed 2010 under the TNEB restructuring (Tamil Nadu Electricity (Reorganisation and Reforms) Transfer Scheme)
how.act_no: Electricity Act, 2003 (Central Act 36 of 2003); TANGEDCO incorporated 2010

why.stated: Electricity-sector reform: unbundling generation/transmission/distribution into corporatised entities for commercial efficiency, mandated by the Electricity Act 2003.
real_political_economy: Neoliberal conditionality (Cooper): the Electricity Act 2003 imposed the unbundling/corporatisation template nationally as the precondition for reform-linked funds — a central conditionality reshaping a state utility.

Power was never a municipal function in Chennai, but its corporatised, regulator-governed form (TNERC, not the ballot) is the same democratic-deficit logic: the citizen is a captive consumer regulated, not represented.
Counter-pattern worth surfacing: Chennai kept electricity PUBLIC (state) where peer cities privatised it — a rare non-private carve-out.

carve_outs.source: Electricity Act 2003; TNEB unbundling 2010 (TANGEDCO/TANTRANSCO); service_providers.json (electricity = TANGEDCO, state_dept).

carve_outs.body: Urbaser-Sumeet (Urbaser SA, Spain + Sumeet Group, India)
carve_outs.function_taken: Solid-waste management OPERATION — door-to-door collection, transport, conservancy across ~7 GCC zones (zones 9-15), ~half the city
carve_outs.what: Private concessionaire operating solid-waste management and conservancy across 7 of the GCC's 15 zones (~207 sq km, ~3.7M people, 92 wards). The corporation's flagship in-house function — conservancy/SWM, the bread-and-butter that the most-hollowed corporation still nominally 'runs' — is operationally privatised across half the city.

how.instrument: 8-year O&M concession contract awarded by the Greater Chennai Corporation (with TN state government approval), signed October 2020, ~EUR 480 million; awarded under the corporation's contracting powers within the state-set framework
how.act_no: Concession contract (not a statute); SWM duty derives from the Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986

why.stated: Efficiency, mechanisation, and improved cleanliness/Swachh-survey performance via a specialised private operator with capital and fleet.
real_political_economy: Caste/labour offloading (Ambedkar): the predominantly-Dalit, predominantly-women conservancy workforce was transferred from GCC rolls to the private firm, extinguishing a long struggle for permanent municipal employment and CUTTING take-home pay (~Rs 11,730 -> ~Rs 9,000/mo). Contractualisation as a caste-precarity machine.

Cooper's counterrevolution: privatising the OPERATION of a core public service hollows the elected body's last large in-house estate; the corporation becomes a contract-administering shell even where it scores 'green' on the scorecard.
Cross-party complicity: the privatisation proceeded under both DMK and AIADMK state governments — a bipartisan state project, not a city decision (the GCC council had no meaningful veto).

carve_outs.source: contractualization_map.json (chennai.solid_waste_collection); Citizen Matters; The News Minute; CenFA 'A Big Step Back for Chennai's Conservancy Workers'; The South First.

carve_outs.function_taken: Solid-waste management OPERATION — conservancy/SWM across ~4 GCC zones; with Urbaser, 10 of 15 GCC zones under private operators by July 2025
carve_outs.what: Private concessionaire operating SWM/conservancy across ~4 of the GCC's 15 zones. Together with Urbaser-Sumeet (7 zones), Ramky brings the privatised total to 10 of 15 zones (two-thirds of the city) by July 2025, with Royapuram and Thiru Vi Ka Nagar slated for transfer next.

how.instrument: O&M concession contract(s) awarded by the Greater Chennai Corporation (state-approved); awarded under corporation contracting powers within the state framework
how.act_no: Concession contract (not a statute); SWM duty under SWM Rules 2016 / Environment (Protection) Act 1986

why.stated: Same as Urbaser: mechanised, specialised private conservancy for efficiency and cleanliness-survey ranking.
real_political_economy: The tipping point: with Ramky's zones, 10/15 GCC zones are privately operated — the most extensive large-city conservancy privatisation in the atlas. The elected corporation's single biggest in-house function is now majority-private.
Caste/labour offloading: same worker transfer and pay-cut dynamics; the front line moves from municipal to contract status across two-thirds of the city.

Ghosh's corporate municipality, completed: the body keeps the broom only nominally — the rent (collection fees, processing) and the operation are the concessionaire's; the city holds liability and oversight without control.

carve_outs.source: contractualization_map.json (chennai; 'By July 2025, 10 of 15 zones under private operators'); Citizen Matters; CenFA.

boundary_note.what: The 2011 'Greater Chennai' expansion — the corporation's own territory was redrawn by the STATE, not the council.
boundary_note.detail: In October 2011, 42 local bodies (9 municipalities incl. Ambattur, Alandur, Tiruvottiyur, Madhavaram, Maduravoyal, Valasaravakkam, plus town panchayats and panchayat unions) were merged into the corporation, more than doubling it from ~174 km²/155 wards to 426 km²/200 wards/15 zones (creating today's Greater Chennai Corporation).

how.instrument: Government notification under the Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919 — NOT a fresh statute
how.act_no: Executive notification under TN Act IV of 1919

boundary_note.significance: Even the elected corporation's boundary is drawn by state executive fiat under the 1919 Act, not by the council. The 'GCC' brand of 2011 is a state notification, not municipal self-determination. (Correction to a common ' 2021-22' framing, which conflates the 2011 expansion with the 2022 local-body elections — see laws/chennai/manifest.md.)
boundary_note.source: data/laws/chennai/manifest.md (2011 expansion by notification under the 1919 Act).

summary.bodies_and_instruments: CMDA (1972), CMWSSB/Metrowater (1978), TN Slum Clearance Board (1970), TN Housing Board (1961), MTC (1972), CMRL (2007), Chennai Smart City Ltd (2016), TANGEDCO (2010, non-12th-Schedule), Urbaser-Sumeet SWM concession (2020), Ramky SWM concession (2021); plus the 2011 boundary notification.

decided_by_breakdown.note: ZERO carve-outs decided by the elected city. State: CMDA, CMWSSB, TNSCB, TNHB, MTC, Urbaser, Ramky (SWM concessions awarded by GCC but under state approval/framework, no council veto). Centre: CMRL (Centre-State SPV), Chennai Smart City Ltd (Mission conditionality), TANGEDCO (Electricity Act 2003 template). The boundary notification (2011) = state. The founding charter (1688) = colonial.

summary.headline: Chennai holds the OLDEST corporation in India (Madras, 1688) yet is among the MOST hollowed — water, sewerage, planning, land, housing-the-poor, buses, metro, smart-city projects, and now 10 of 15 solid-waste zones all taken from the elected city. In every case the decider was the state government or the Centre; NOT once the elected council. Age did not protect devolution; depoliticisation, land financialisation and (latterly) caste-coded contractualisation did the hollowing — by state and central design.
